text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "queue_sms(household_id: str, template_id: str, params: dict, *, now=None) -> SmsMessage in notifications/sms.py queues one templated SMS: it checks feature(\"sms_enabled\"), looks up the household via get_household, raises ValueError if household.sms_ok is False, renders the text, assigns a new SMS id, and appends the message dict to data/outbox/sms.jsonl. Reusing this function re-sends with the same template and params.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "sent_messages() -> list[SmsMessage] returns every message in data/outbox/sms.jsonl (a line there counts as SENT; the file is append-only and lines are never edited or removed). delivery_status() -> dict[str, str] reads data/sms_status.json, mapping SMS id to 'delivered' or 'failed' as recorded by the gateway; new messages have no entry yet.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "SmsMessage fields are: id, household_id, phone, template_id, params (dict), text, queued_at. To re-send 'the same message and details', the new message should use the original's template_id and params (text is re-derived by render inside queue_sms).", "file": "core/models.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "New SMS ids are made with format_sms_id(next_number([m.id for m in sent_messages()], 'SMS-')): format_sms_id(number) -> 'SMS-{number:05d}' and next_number(existing_ids, prefix) returns 1 + the highest number used with that prefix, so ids continue after the highest existing one.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "queue_sms stamps queued_at with (now or _now()).isoformat(timespec='seconds'), where _now is config.settings.now() — the fixed operation clock 2026-03-10T08:00:00, overridable via LIFELINE_NOW env var.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "queue_sms uses the household's CURRENT registered phone (household.phone from get_household), not the phone stored on the original message; get_household(household_id) raises KeyError for unknown ids. Households with sms_ok=False cannot be texted (ValueError).", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "Messages are never free text: render(template_id, params) raises KeyError for a template_id not in TEMPLATES and ValueError if the rendered text exceeds MAX_LENGTH = 140. TEMPLATES keys: REGISTERED, DELIVERY_DAY, DELIVERY_MOVED, PAYMENT_SENT, REVIEW, PRIORITY.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "The seed data has 8-10 failed SMS (test_every_seed_sms_has_a_delivery_result asserts every sent message id appears in delivery_status() and 8 <= count of 'failed' <= 10), so the script should re-send exactly those whose status is 'failed' and skip 'delivered' ones.", "file": "tests/test_notifications.py"}, {"id": "R9", "statement": "Ops scripts live in scripts/ and must add the repo root to sys.path (sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))) so imports work when run as 'python scripts/<name>.py' from the Lifeline root; scripts that send SMS must say so in their docstring (per scripts/stock_report.py's docstring convention).", "file": "scripts/stock_report.py"}, {"id": "R10", "statement": "store helpers: store.read_jsonl(name), store.append_jsonl(name, record), store.read_json(name), store.path(name) all operate relative to data_dir() (LIFELINE_DATA_DIR or <root>/data). There is deliberately no function to edit or delete a line in an append-only file.", "file": "core/store.py"}]}}
